newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour's Brown says will "take on" monopolies.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour's Brown says will "take on" monopolies.

text.p: UK opposition Labour Party finance spokesman Gordon Brown said on Monday a Labour government would tackle "boardroom excesses within the privatised monopolies."

"We will not only set an inflation target but I will take on those monopolies who abuse their power to force prices up," Brown said on Monday in a speech prepared for delivery at the Labour Party's annual conference in Blackpool.

"A Labour Chancellor will not waste money on nursery vouchers, on the quango state, on tax relief for boardroom excesses within the privatised monopolies, and on indiscriminate handouts of public money to undervalued rail companies that should never have been privatised," he said.
Brown added that the Post Office should not be privatised and should remain a public service in the public sector.
He attacked the Conservative government for "a crude free market ideology based on the narrow pursuit of self-interest of the few at the expense of the many."
